Negative results and failure knowledge

Screens 12–16. The differentiator. The field research found 71% of surveyed researchers would submit negative results and 0% follow an existing negative-results platform — so the design assumption is that willingness is not the problem and destination is. A null result here is a structured object inside the workflow the researcher already uses, not a submission to a separate venue.

You are publishing a contribution, not admitting a failure.
This gets a DOI, a version, a licence and a place on your Replication axis — the same treatment as any dataset. It is orange here and everywhere, never red: red is for system errors, and a result that reproduces is not an error.

4 · WHAT HAPPENED
Efficiency stayed at 4 ± 1% across all nine wells, in both lots, at all three passages. Viability was above 92% throughout. The fresh prep and the new lot changed nothing.

5 · WHAT THIS RULES OUTthe field that makes it reusable
Reagent lot as the cause of the passage cliff — two lots, same result
Plasmid quality / endotoxin — fresh prep at 0.04 EU/µg, no recovery
Simple cell death — viability above 92% in every well
?Does not rule out receptor loss, CO₂ drift, or anything about other cell lines. Saying what you did not test is part of the object.

WHAT PUBLISHING DOES
Mints a DOI
Citable in a paper, a grant report or a thesis. Counts as an output on your CV export.
Attaches to MC-0288 as a failed run
The next person to open that card sees your result in its failure modes. That is where it will actually be found.
Enters the failure taxonomy
Filed under sample → passage effects, where people browse for exactly this.
Moves your Replication axis
+12. Null results are a scored axis, not a rounding error.
WHAT IT DOES NOT DO
It does not contradict MC-0288 or reflect on T. Okafor. A method that fails outside its stated range is a method with a known boundary, which is better than a method with an unknown one.

WHY A TAXONOMY AND NOT TAGS
Tags describe what a result is about. The taxonomy describes what broke. Six causes, fixed, so a failure filed in one lab is findable by a lab that would never have used the same words for it.
THE BRANCH WE WATCH
Sample is the largest branch and the one where duplicated work is most expensive — a mis-identified line invalidates everything downstream. It is also where a single well-powered null result saves the most weeks.

WHY PER MODEL
Instrument failures are the most transferable knowledge in science and the least written down — they live in a core facility's head. One hub per model makes them additive across institutions.
WHAT IS NOT HERE
No vendor content, no marketing, no service contracts. If a vendor engineer answers, they are labelled as one.
